title.zh: 卷八十二 列傳第三十二: 許敬宗 李義府
title.en: Volume 82 Biographies 32: Xu Jingzong, Li Yifu
title.raw: 卷八十二 列傳第三十二: 許敬宗 李義府 Volume 82 Biographies 32: Xu Jingzong, Li Yifu

sentences.zh: 許敬宗

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong

sentences.zh: 許敬宗，杭州新城人，隋禮部侍郎善心子也。

translations.literal: Xu Jingzong was a man of Xincheng in Hangzhou, and was the son of Shanshan, Vice Minister of Rites of the Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Xu Jingzong, a native of Xincheng in Hangzhou, was the son of Shanshan, who had served the Sui as Vice Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 其先自高陽南渡，世仕江左。

translations.literal: His ancestors crossed south from Gaoyang, and for generations served in Jiangzuo.
translations.idiomatic: His family had crossed south from Gaoyang and for generations held office in the lands south of the Yangtze.

sentences.zh: 敬宗幼善屬文，舉秀才，授淮陽郡司法書佐，俄直謁者台，奏通事舍人事。

translations.literal: Jingzong in youth was skilled at literary composition, passed the xiucai examination, was appointed judicial clerk of Huaiyang commandery, and soon served on the Direct Petitioners Board and memorialized for the post of Master of Ceremonies Concierge.
translations.idiomatic: As a youth Jingzong excelled at literary composition. He passed the xiucai examination and was appointed judicial clerk of Huaiyang commandery; before long he served on the Direct Petitioners Board and petitioned for appointment as Master of Ceremonies Concierge.

sentences.zh: 江都之難，善心為宇文化及所害。

translations.literal: At the catastrophe of Jiangdu, Shanshan was killed by Yuwen Huaji.
translations.idiomatic: During the upheaval at Jiangdu, Shanshan was killed by Yuwen Huaji.

sentences.zh: 敬宗流轉，投於李密，密以為元帥府記室，與魏徵同為管記。

translations.literal: Jingzong wandered about and attached himself to Li Mi; Mi made him secretary of the Marshal's Headquarters, and together with Wei Zheng he served as record-keeper.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong wandered from place to place until he joined Li Mi, who appointed him secretary in the Marshal's Headquarters, where he and Wei Zheng shared duties as record-keepers.

sentences.zh: 武德初，赤牒擬漣州別駕。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Wude, a red patent named him acting prefect of Lianzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Wude reign a red patent named him acting prefect of Lianzhou.

sentences.zh: 太宗聞其名，召補秦府學士。

translations.literal: Taizong heard his name and summoned him to serve as a scholar in the Prince of Qin's household.
translations.idiomatic: When the future Emperor Taizong heard of him, he summoned Jingzong to serve as a scholar in the Prince of Qin's household.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，累除著作郎，兼修國史，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan he was repeatedly promoted to Gentleman of the Writing Office, concurrently compiled the national history, and was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Zhenguan era he rose through successive posts to Gentleman of the Writing Office, served concurrently as compiler of the national history, and was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 十年，文德皇后崩，百官縗絰。

translations.literal: In the tenth year the Wende Empress died, and all officials wore mourning hemp.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year Empress Wende died, and the entire bureaucracy went into mourning dress.

sentences.zh: 率更令歐陽詢狀貌醜異，眾或指之，敬宗見而大笑，為御史所劾，左授洪州都督府司馬。

translations.literal: The Director of the Bureau of Weights and Measures Ouyang Xun had an ugly and peculiar appearance; the crowd sometimes pointed at him, and when Jingzong saw this he burst out laughing. The censorate impeached him, and he was demoted to army adjutant of the Hongzhou area command.
translations.idiomatic: Ouyang Xun, Director of the Bureau of Weights and Measures, had a grotesque appearance, and people in the crowd would sometimes point at him. When Jingzong saw this he laughed aloud. The censorate impeached him, and he was demoted to army adjutant under the Hongzhou area command.

sentences.zh: 累遷給事中，兼修國史。

translations.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to Attendant Within the Gates, and concurrently compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: He was promoted in stages to Attendant Within the Gates while continuing to compile the national history.

sentences.zh: 十七年，以修《武德》、《貞觀實錄》成，封高陽縣男，賜物八百段，權檢校黃門侍郎。

translations.literal: In the seventeenth year, because the compilation of the Veritable Records of Wude and Zhenguan was completed, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang county, granted eight hundred bolts of goods, and given acting authority as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventeenth year, when the Veritable Records of the Wude and Zhenguan reigns were finished, he was enfeoffed as Baron of Gaoyang, rewarded with eight hundred bolts of silk and goods, and given acting authority as Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 高宗在春宮，遷太子右庶子。

translations.literal: When Gaozong was in the Eastern Palace, Jingzong was transferred to Right Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: While Gaozong was still crown prince, Jingzong was appointed Right Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 十九年，太宗親伐高麗，皇太子定州監國，敬宗與高士廉等共知機要。

translations.literal: In the nineteenth year Taizong personally attacked Goguryeo; the crown prince supervised the state at Dingzhou, and Jingzong together with Gao Shilian and others jointly handled confidential affairs.
translations.idiomatic: In the nineteenth year Emperor Taizong led a campaign against Goguryeo in person. The crown prince remained at Dingzhou to oversee the realm, and Jingzong joined Gao Shilian and others in managing confidential state affairs.

sentences.zh: 中書令岑文本卒於行所，令敬宗以本官檢校中書侍郎。

translations.literal: Chief Secretariat Counselor Cen Wende died on campaign, and Jingzong was ordered to act as Vice Minister of the Secretariat while retaining his original post.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Secretariat Counselor Cen Wende died on campaign, and Jingzong was ordered to act as Vice Minister of the Secretariat while keeping his existing rank.

sentences.zh: 太宗大破遼賊於駐蹕山，敬宗立於馬前受旨草詔書，詞彩甚麗，深見嗟賞。

translations.literal: Taizong inflicted a great defeat on the Liaodong rebels at Zhubi Mountain; Jingzong stood before his horse to receive orders and draft an edict, the diction and color of which were very beautiful, and he was deeply praised.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Taizong routed the Liaodong forces at Zhubi Mountain, Jingzong stood at his horse's head to receive orders and draft an edict on the spot. The prose was so polished that the emperor admired it warmly.

sentences.zh: 先是，庶人承乾廢黜，宮僚多被除削，久未收敘。

translations.literal: Earlier, when the commoner Chengqian was deposed, many palace staff were dismissed and stripped of rank, and for a long time had not been restored to office.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, after the deposed heir Chengqian was reduced to commoner status, many of his former palace staff had been dismissed and stripped of rank, and for years none had been restored to office.

sentences.zh: 敬宗上表曰：「臣聞先王慎罰，務在於恤刑，往哲寬仁，義在於宥過。

translations.literal: Jingzong submitted a memorial saying: "Your servant has heard that the former kings were cautious in punishment and strove to show compassion in penal affairs; the sages of old were lenient and humane, and their principle lay in pardoning faults."
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong submitted a memorial that read: "I have heard that the ancient kings were cautious in imposing punishments and strove above all to temper justice with mercy, and that the sages of old were lenient and humane because their purpose was to pardon faults."

sentences.zh: 聖人之道，莫尚於茲。

translations.literal: In the Way of the sages nothing is more exalted than this.
translations.idiomatic: Nothing in the Way of the sages stands higher than this principle.

sentences.zh: 竊見廢官，五品以上，除名棄斥，頗歷歲時。

translations.literal: Your servant has observed that dismissed officials of the fifth rank and above, whose names were struck from the rolls and who were cast out, have already passed considerable time.
translations.idiomatic: I observe that dismissed officials of the fifth rank and above, whose names were struck from the rolls and who were cast out in disgrace, have already endured many years in exile.

sentences.zh: 但庶人疇昔之年，身處不疑之地，苞藏悖逆，陰結宰臣，所預奸謀，多連宗戚。

translations.literal: Yet in years past the commoner, while occupying a position free from suspicion, harbored rebellion and secretly joined with chief ministers; the treacherous plots in which he was involved mostly implicated his kinsmen by marriage and clan.
translations.idiomatic: Yet in years past the deposed heir, though he stood in a position that ought to have been above suspicion, harbored treason and secretly conspired with chief ministers. The plots in which he took part mostly involved his own kin and affines.

sentences.zh: 禍生慮表，非可防萌，宮內官僚，迥無關預。

translations.literal: Disaster arose beyond what could be foreseen and could not be prevented at the sprouting stage; the palace officials had nothing at all to do with it.
translations.idiomatic: The disaster arose beyond what anyone could have foreseen at its first stirrings and could not have been stopped in advance. The palace officials had no part in it whatsoever.

sentences.zh: 今乃投鼠及器，孰謂無冤？

translations.literal: Now one casts the rat and hits the vessel as well—who would say there is no injustice?
translations.idiomatic: Yet now the rat is thrown and the vessel is struck as well. Who could call this free of injustice?

sentences.zh: 焚山毀玉，稍同遷怒。

translations.literal: To burn the mountain and destroy the jade is somewhat like venting anger on the wrong target.
translations.idiomatic: To burn the mountain and destroy the jade along with it is much like venting one's anger on the innocent.

sentences.zh: 伏尋先典，例有可原。

translations.literal: Your servant has examined the former canons and finds that precedent allows forgiveness.
translations.idiomatic: When I examine the precedents of antiquity, I find case after case in which pardon was granted.

sentences.zh: 昔吳國陪臣，則爰絲不坐於劉濞；

translations.literal: In former times, among the attendant ministers of the state of Wu, Yuan Si was not punished for Liu Pi's crime;
translations.idiomatic: In former times Yuan Si, an attendant minister of Wu, was not punished for the crime of Liu Pi;

sentences.zh: 昌邑中尉，則王吉免緣於海昏。

translations.literal: the commandant of Changyi, Wang Ji, was spared on account of the Marquis of Haihun.
translations.idiomatic: and Wang Ji, commandant of Changyi, was spared any connection with the Marquis of Haihun's guilt.

sentences.zh: 譬諸欒布，乃策名於彭越；

translations.literal: Compare Luan Bu, who nevertheless made his name under Peng Yue;
translations.idiomatic: Consider Luan Bu, who nevertheless won his place under Peng Yue;

sentences.zh: 比乎田叔，亦委質於張敖。

translations.literal: or Tian Shu, who likewise pledged himself to Zhang Ao.
translations.idiomatic: or Tian Shu, who likewise pledged his service to Zhang Ao.

sentences.zh: 主以凶逆，陷其誅夷；

translations.literal: Their lords because of treason fell into execution and extermination;
translations.idiomatic: Their lords, convicted of treason, were executed and their houses destroyed;

sentences.zh: 臣以賢良，荷彼收擢。

translations.literal: the subjects because of worth were favored with recruitment and promotion.
translations.idiomatic: yet the subjects themselves, judged worthy, were taken up and promoted.

sentences.zh: 歷觀往代，此類尤多。

translations.literal: Surveying past ages, cases of this kind are especially numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Looking back through the ages, examples of this kind are especially numerous.

sentences.zh: 近者有隋，又遵斯義。

translations.literal: In recent times the Sui again followed this principle.
translations.idiomatic: The Sui dynasty, not long ago, followed the same principle.

sentences.zh: 楊勇之廢，罪止加於佞人，李綱之徒，皆不預於刑網。

translations.literal: When Yang Yong was deposed, guilt fell only on the flatterers; men such as Li Gang were none of them caught in the penal net.
translations.idiomatic: When Yang Yong was deposed, punishment fell only on the flatterers around him. Men such as Li Gang were never caught in the penal net.

sentences.zh: 古今裁其折衷，史籍稱為美談。

translations.literal: Ancient and modern judged the mean between extremes in this way, and the historical records praise it as a fine story.
translations.idiomatic: Ancient and modern alike have weighed such cases in the balance, and the histories praise them as exemplary acts of justice.

sentences.zh: 而今張玄素、令狐德棻、趙弘智、裴宣機、蕭鈞等，並砥節勵操，有雅望於當朝；

translations.literal: But now Zhang Xuansu, Linghu Defen, Zhao Hongzhi, Pei Xuanji, Xiao Jun, and others all sharpen their integrity and strengthen their conduct, and enjoy refined repute in the present court;
translations.idiomatic: Yet today Zhang Xuansu, Linghu Defen, Zhao Hongzhi, Pei Xuanji, Xiao Jun, and others have all polished their integrity and strengthened their conduct, and enjoy high repute at court;

sentences.zh: 經明行修，播令名於天下。

translations.literal: they are versed in the classics and cultivated in conduct, and spread a fine name throughout the realm.
translations.idiomatic: they are versed in the classics and exemplary in conduct, and their good names are known throughout the realm.

sentences.zh: 或以直言而遭箠撲，或以忤意而見猜嫌，一概雷同，並罹天憲，恐於王道，傷在未弘。

translations.literal: Some because of blunt speech suffered beating, some because of offending the will were viewed with suspicion; treated all alike in identical fashion, they together fell under heaven's law. I fear that for the kingly Way the harm lies in its not being broad enough.
translations.idiomatic: Some were beaten for speaking bluntly, others were suspected for giving offense. Treated all alike without distinction, they have alike fallen under imperial punishment. I fear that for the kingly Way the harm lies in its not being broad enough.

sentences.zh: 」由是玄素等稍得敘用。

translations.literal: " Thereupon Xuansu and the others gradually obtained restoration to office.
translations.idiomatic: " As a result Xuansu and the others were gradually restored to office.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，加銀青光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year he was given the additional title Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year he was given the additional title Silver-Gleam Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，代於志寧為禮部尚書。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Jingzong replaced Yu Zhining as Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Jingzong replaced Yu Zhining as Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嫁女與蠻酋馮盎之子，多納金寶，為有司所劾，左授鄭州刺史。

translations.literal: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to the son of the barbarian chieftain Feng Ang and accepted many golds and treasures; the responsible offices impeached him, and he was demoted to prefect of Zhengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to the son of the tribal chieftain Feng Ang and accepted a large payment in gold and jewels. The responsible offices impeached him, and he was demoted to prefect of Zhengzhou.

sentences.zh: 永徽三年，入為衛尉卿，加弘文館學士，兼修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year of Yonghui he entered the capital as Minister of the Guard, was given the additional post of Scholar of the Hongwen Institute, and concurrently compiled the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of the Yonghui era he was recalled to the capital as Minister of the Guard, made a Scholar of the Hongwen Institute, and again charged with compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 六年，復拜禮部尚書，高宗將廢皇后王氏而立武昭儀，敬宗特贊成其計。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was again appointed Minister of Rites. Gaozong was about to depose Empress Wang and establish Lady Wu as consort; Jingzong especially supported the plan.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was again appointed Minister of Rites. When Emperor Gaozong planned to depose Empress Wang and install Lady Wu as consort, Jingzong strongly backed the scheme.

sentences.zh: 長孫無忌、褚遂良、韓瑗等並直言忤旨，敬宗與李義府潛加誣構，並流死於嶺外。

translations.literal: Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and others all spoke bluntly against the imperial will; Jingzong and Li Yifu secretly added false charges, and they were all exiled and died beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Zhangsun Wuji, Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, and others all spoke bluntly against the emperor's will. Jingzong and Li Yifu secretly fabricated charges against them, and they were all exiled to the far south, where they died.

sentences.zh: 顯慶元年，加太子賓客，尋冊拜侍中，監修國史。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianqing he was given the additional post of Guest of the Heir Apparent; soon he was appointed by patent as Palace Attendant and supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xianqing era he was made Guest of the Heir Apparent, and soon afterward was appointed Palace Attendant and put in charge of compiling the national history.

sentences.zh: 三年，進封郡公，尋贈其父善心為冀州刺史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was advanced to enfeoffment as Duke of a commandery; soon his father Shanshan was posthumously given the post of prefect of Jizhou.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was advanced to Duke of a commandery, and soon afterward his father Shanshan was posthumously appointed prefect of Jizhou.

sentences.zh: 高宗因於古長安城遊覽，問侍臣曰：「朕觀故城舊基，宮室似與百姓雜居，自秦、漢已來，幾代都此？

translations.literal: Gaozong while touring the old Chang'an city asked his attendant ministers: "We observe the old foundations of the former city; the palaces seem to have been mixed with the common people in residence. Since Qin and Han, how many dynasties have made this their capital?"
translations.idiomatic: While touring the old Chang'an city, Emperor Gaozong asked his ministers: "I see the old foundations here. The palaces seem to have stood mingled with ordinary dwellings. Since Qin and Han times, how many dynasties have used this place as their capital?"

sentences.zh: 」敬宗對曰：「秦都咸陽，郭邑連跨渭水，故云『渭水貫都，以象天河。

translations.literal: " Jingzong replied: "The Qin capital was at Xianyang; the outer walls and wards stretched across the Wei River, hence the saying 'The Wei River runs through the capital, symbolizing the River of Heaven.'"
translations.idiomatic: " Jingzong replied: "The Qin capital was at Xianyang, and its outer wards stretched across the Wei River. Hence the saying, 'The Wei River runs through the capital, like the River of Heaven across the sky.'"

sentences.zh: 』至漢惠帝始築此城，其後苻堅、姚萇、後周並都之。

translations.literal: " It was Emperor Hui of Han who first built this city; afterward Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and the Later Zhou all made it their capital."
translations.idiomatic: " Emperor Hui of Han was the first to build this city. Later Fu Jian, Yao Chang, and the Northern Zhou all made it their capital as well."

sentences.zh: 」帝又問：「昆明池是漢武帝何年中開鑿？

translations.literal: " The emperor further asked: "In which year of Emperor Wu of Han was Kunming Pool excavated?"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then asked: "In which year of Emperor Wu of Han was Kunming Pool excavated?"

sentences.zh: 」敬宗對曰：「武帝遣使通西南夷，而為昆明滇池所閉，欲伐昆明國，故因鎬之舊澤，以穿此池，用習水戰，元狩三年事也。

translations.literal: " Jingzong replied: "Emperor Wu sent envoys to open relations with the southwestern Yi, but they were blocked by the Kunming Pool of Dian; wishing to attack the state of Kunming, he therefore followed the old marshlands of the Jing River region to cut this pool for practicing naval warfare. This was in the third year of Yuanshuo."
translations.idiomatic: " Jingzong replied: "Emperor Wu sent envoys to open relations with the peoples of the southwest, but they were blocked by the waters of Lake Dian near Kunming. Wishing to campaign against the Kunming state, he followed the old marshlands of the Jing River basin to cut this pool and train his forces in naval warfare. That was in the third year of the Yuanshuo era."

sentences.zh: 」帝因令敬宗與弘文館學士具檢秦、漢已來歷代宮室處所以奏。

translations.literal: " The emperor thereupon ordered Jingzong and the scholars of the Hongwen Institute to compile and examine the sites of palaces of successive dynasties since Qin and Han and memorialize the results.
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor then ordered Jingzong and the scholars of the Hongwen Institute to research and report on the palace sites of every dynasty since Qin and Han times.

sentences.zh: 其年，代李義府為中書令，任遇之重，當朝莫比。

translations.literal: That year he replaced Li Yifu as Chief Secretariat Counselor; the weight of his appointment and favor was unmatched in the court of the day.
translations.idiomatic: That year he replaced Li Yifu as Chief Secretariat Counselor. No one at court enjoyed greater favor or heavier responsibility.

sentences.zh: 龍朔二年，從新令改為右相，加光祿大夫。

translations.literal: In the second year of Longshuo, under the new statutes he was changed to Right Chancellor and given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Longshuo era, under the new administrative statutes he was redesignated Right Chancellor and given the additional title Grand Master of Splendid Happiness.

sentences.zh: 三年，冊拜太子少師、同東西台三品，並依舊監修國史。

translations.literal: In the third year he was appointed by patent as Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Third Rank equal to the Eastern and Western Offices, and as before supervised compilation of the national history.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was appointed Junior Tutor of the Heir Apparent and Third Rank with equal standing on the Eastern and Western Offices, while continuing as before to supervise compilation of the national history.

sentences.zh: 乾封初，以敬宗年老，不能行步，特令與司空李勣，每朝日各乘小馬入禁門至內省。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Qianfeng, because Jingzong was old and could not walk, he was specially ordered together with the Minister of Works Li Ji that on each court day they should each ride a small horse through the forbidden gate to the inner offices.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Qianfeng era, because Jingzong was elderly and could no longer walk easily, a special order was issued that he and Minister of Works Li Ji might each ride a pony through the forbidden gate to the inner offices on days of court audience.

sentences.zh: 敬宗自掌知國史，記事阿曲。

translations.literal: Jingzong personally took charge of the national history and recorded events in a flattering and distorted manner.
translations.idiomatic: Once Jingzong took personal charge of the national history, he recorded events in a flattering and distorted manner.

sentences.zh: 初，虞世基與敬宗父善心同為宇文化及所害，封德彝時為內史舍人，備見其事，因謂人曰：「世基被誅，世南匍匐而請代；

translations.literal: Earlier, Yu Shiji and Jingzong's father Shanshan were both killed by Yuwen Huaji. Feng Deyi was then Secretariat Drafter and witnessed the whole affair in detail, and therefore said to people: "When Shiji was condemned to execution, Shinan crawled prostrate to beg to take his place;
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, Yu Shiji and Jingzong's father Shanshan had both been killed by Yuwen Huaji. Feng Deyi was then a Secretariat drafter and witnessed the whole affair. He later told others: "When Shiji was condemned to death, his brother Shinan crawled forward on his knees to beg to die in his place;

sentences.zh: 善心之死，敬宗舞蹈以求生。

translations.literal: when Shanshan died, Jingzong danced and capered to save his life."
translations.idiomatic: when Shanshan faced death, Jingzong danced and capered to save his own life."

sentences.zh: 」人以為口實，敬宗深銜之，及為德彝立傳，盛加其罪惡。

translations.literal: " People took this as a byword; Jingzong deeply resented it, and when he wrote a biography for Deyi he heaped up his crimes and wickedness.
translations.idiomatic: " People repeated this story for years. Jingzong bore a deep grudge against Feng Deyi, and when he came to write Deyi's biography he piled on accusations of crime and wickedness.

sentences.zh: 敬宗嫁女與左監門大將軍錢九隴，本皇家隸人，敬宗貪財與婚，乃為九隴曲敘門閥，妄加功績，並升與劉文靜、長孫順德同卷。

translations.literal: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to Qian Jiulong, General of the Left Gate Guards, who was originally a bondservant of the imperial house. Jingzong, greedy for wealth, entered the marriage alliance and therefore for Jiulong bent the narrative of his lineage, falsely added achievements, and elevated him to the same fascicle as Liu Wenjing and Zhangsun Shunde.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong gave his daughter in marriage to Qian Jiulong, General of the Left Gate Guards, who had originally been a bondservant of the imperial house. Greedy for the bride-price, Jingzong bent Jiulong's genealogy to flatter him, invented achievements for him, and placed his biography in the same fascicle as those of Liu Wenjing and Zhangsun Shunde.

sentences.zh: 敬宗為子娶尉遲寶琳孫女為妻，多得賂遺，及作寶琳父敬德傳，悉為隱諸過咎。

translations.literal: Jingzong had his son take as wife the granddaughter of Yuchi Baolin and received many bribes and gifts; when he wrote the biography of Baolin's father Jingde, he concealed all his faults and errors.
translations.idiomatic: He arranged for his son to marry the granddaughter of Yuchi Baolin and accepted a large bride-price. When he wrote the biography of Baolin's father Jingde, he concealed every fault and failing.

sentences.zh: 太宗作《威鳳賦》以賜長孫無忌，敬宗改雲賜敬德。

translations.literal: Taizong composed the "Rhapsody on the Majestic Phoenix" to bestow on Zhangsun Wuji; Jingzong altered it to say it was bestowed on Jingde.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Taizong had composed the "Rhapsody on the Majestic Phoenix" as a gift to Zhangsun Wuji, but Jingzong altered the record to say it had been given to Jingde instead.

sentences.zh: 白州人龐孝泰，蠻酋凡品，率兵從征高麗，賊知其懦，襲破之。

translations.literal: Pang Xiaotai of Baizhou, a barbarian chieftain of ordinary rank, led troops on campaign against Goguryeo; the enemy knew he was weak and raided and defeated him.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xiaotai of Baizhou, a tribal chieftain of no distinction, led troops on the campaign against Goguryeo. The enemy knew he was timid and routed his force.

sentences.zh: 敬宗又納其寶貨，稱孝泰頻破賊徒，斬獲數萬。

translations.literal: Jingzong again accepted his treasures and goods and declared that Xiaotai repeatedly defeated the rebel bands and beheaded and captured tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong accepted bribes from him and recorded that Xiaotai had repeatedly routed the enemy and taken tens of thousands of heads and captives.

sentences.zh: 漢將驍健者，唯蘇定方與龐孝泰耳，曹繼叔、劉伯英皆出其下。

translations.literal: Among Han generals who were valiant and strong, only Su Dingfang and Pang Xiaotai; Cao Jishu and Liu Boying were both beneath them.
translations.idiomatic: Among the valiant Han commanders of the day, he wrote, only Su Dingfang and Pang Xiaotai stood at the top, while Cao Jishu and Liu Boying ranked below them.

sentences.zh: 虛美隱惡如此！

translations.literal: To inflate merit and conceal evil in this way!
translations.idiomatic: Such was the way he inflated merit and concealed wrongdoing!

sentences.zh: 初，高祖、太宗兩朝實錄，其敬播所修者，頗多詳直，敬宗又輒以己愛憎曲事刪改，論者尤之。

translations.literal: At first, in the Veritable Records of the two reigns of Gaozu and Taizong, the portions compiled by Jing Bo were in many places detailed and straight; Jingzong again arbitrarily deleted and altered events according to his own likes and dislikes, and critics especially faulted him for this.
translations.idiomatic: The Veritable Records of the Gaozu and Taizong reigns, in the portions compiled by Jing Bo, had been detailed and forthright in many places. Jingzong then arbitrarily cut and altered events to suit his own likes and dislikes, and critics especially condemned him for it.

sentences.zh: 然自貞觀已來，朝廷所修《五代史》及《晉書》、《東殿新書》、《西域圖志》、《文思博要》、《文館詞林》、《累璧》、《瑤山玉彩》《姓氏錄》、《新禮》，皆總知其事，前後賞賚，不可勝紀。

translations.literal: Yet from Zhenguan onward, the court compilations of the History of the Five Dynasties, the Book of Jin, the New Book of the Eastern Hall, the Gazetteer of the Western Regions, the Literary Thoughts Broad Compendium, the Forest of Literary Phrases of the Literary Institute, the Accumulated Jade Tablets, the Jade Splendor of Mount Yao, the Record of Surnames, and the New Rites were all under his general direction, and rewards before and after are beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Yet from the Zhenguan era onward he had overall charge of such court compilations as the History of the Five Dynasties, the Book of Jin, the New Book of the Eastern Hall, the Gazetteer of the Western Regions, the Literary Thoughts Broad Compendium, the Forest of Literary Phrases of the Literary Institute, the Accumulated Jade Tablets, the Jade Splendor of Mount Yao, the Record of Surnames, and the New Rites. The rewards he received over the years were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 敬宗好色無度。

translations.literal: Jingzong was lustful without limit.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong was insatiably lustful.

sentences.zh: 其長子昂頗有才藻，歷位太子舍人。

translations.literal: His eldest son Ang was quite gifted in literary talent and held the post of Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: His eldest son Ang was gifted in letters and had served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 母裴氏早卒。

translations.literal: His mother, the Pei clan, died early.
translations.idiomatic: Ang's mother, of the Pei clan, had died young.

sentences.zh: 裴侍婢有姿色，敬宗嬖之，以為繼室，假姓虞氏。

translations.literal: A maid of the Pei household had beauty; Jingzong favored her, made her his successor wife, and gave her the false surname of the Yu clan.
translations.idiomatic: A maid of the Pei household was beautiful, and Jingzong took her as a favorite and made her his successor wife under the false surname Yu.

sentences.zh: 昂素與通，烝之不絕，敬宗怒黜虞氏，加昂以不孝，奏請流於嶺外。

translations.literal: Ang had long been intimate with her and continued the liaison without cease. Jingzong in anger dismissed the Yu clan woman, charged Ang with lack of filial piety, and memorialized requesting his exile beyond the mountain passes.
translations.idiomatic: Ang had long been intimate with her and continued the affair without cease. Jingzong in anger dismissed the woman of the Yu clan, charged Ang with filial impiety, and memorialized to have him exiled beyond the Lingnan passes.

sentences.zh: 顯慶中，表乞昂還，除虔化令，尋卒。

translations.literal: During Xianqing he submitted a memorial begging that Ang be returned, appointed him magistrate of Qianhua, and soon Ang died.
translations.idiomatic: During the Xianqing era he memorialized to have Ang recalled, appointed him magistrate of Qianhua, and Ang soon died.

sentences.zh: 咸亨元年，抗表乞骸骨，詔聽致仕，仍加特進，俸祿如舊。

translations.literal: In the first year of Xianheng he submitted a memorial resisting service and begging to surrender his bones; an edict permitted his retirement while still granting him Special Advancement, with salary as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Xianheng era he submitted a memorial requesting retirement. An edict granted his request while still conferring Special Advancement on him, with his salary unchanged.

sentences.zh: 三年薨，年八十一。

translations.literal: In the third year he died, at the age of eighty-one.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he died, at the age of eighty-one.

sentences.zh: 高宗為之舉哀，廢朝三日，詔文武百官就第赴哭，冊贈開府儀同三司、揚州大都督，陪葬昭陵。

translations.literal: Gaozong mourned for him, suspended court for three days, ordered civil and military officials of all ranks to go to his residence to attend the lamentation, and by patent posthumously granted him Honorary Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells and Grand Area Commander of Yangzhou, with burial accompaniment at Zhaoling.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Gaozong mourned him in person, suspended court for three days, and ordered civil and military officials of every rank to attend the lamentation at his residence. By patent he was posthumously granted Honorary Grand Master of the Palace with Golden Bells and Grand Area Commander of Yangzhou, with the honor of burial accompaniment at Zhaoling.

sentences.zh: 文集八十捲。

translations.literal: His collected writings were eighty fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to eighty fascicles.

sentences.zh: 太常將定謚，博士袁思古議曰：「敬宗位以才升，歷居清級，然棄長子於荒徼，嫁少女於夷落。

translations.literal: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices was about to fix his posthumous name; Erudite Yuan Sigu proposed: "Jingzong rose in rank through talent and repeatedly held pure offices, yet he abandoned his eldest son in a remote frontier and gave his young daughter in marriage to a barbarian settlement."
translations.idiomatic: When the Court of Imperial Sacrifices was about to fix his posthumous name, Erudite Yuan Sigu proposed: "Jingzong rose through talent and held high office, yet he abandoned his eldest son in a remote frontier and gave his young daughter in marriage to a barbarian settlement."

sentences.zh: 聞《詩》學《禮》，事絕於趨庭；

translations.literal: "He heard the Odes and studied the Rites, yet in practice was cut off from the courtyard instruction;
translations.idiomatic: "He had heard the Odes and studied the Rites, yet in practice he failed the test of instruction in his own courtyard;

sentences.zh: 納采問名，唯聞於黷貨。

translations.literal: in betrothal gifts and asking the name, one heard only of corrupt goods."
translations.idiomatic: and when betrothal gifts were exchanged and the bride's name asked, one heard only of bribes."

sentences.zh: 白圭斯玷，有累清塵，易名之典，須憑實行。

translations.literal: "The white jade has this stain; it weighs upon his pure repute. The canon for changing the name must rely on actual conduct."
translations.idiomatic: "A stain on white jade mars a man's pure reputation. The canon for fixing a posthumous name must rest on actual conduct."

sentences.zh: 按謚法『名與實爽曰繆』，請謚為『繆』。

translations.literal: "According to the canon of posthumous names, 'when name and reality diverge it is called Miu,' and I request the posthumous name Miu."
translations.idiomatic: "By the canon of posthumous names, 'when name and reality diverge, the name is Miu.' I therefore propose the posthumous name Miu."

sentences.zh: 」敬宗孫、太子舍人彥伯不勝其恥，與思古大相忿競，又稱思古與許氏先有嫌隙，請改謚官。

translations.literal: " Jingzong's grandson, Attendant of the Heir Apparent Yanbo, unable to bear the shame, engaged in a great quarrel with Sigu, and further claimed that Sigu had earlier had a grudge against the Xu clan, requesting that the posthumous-name officer be changed.
translations.idiomatic: " Jingzong's grandson Yanbo, who served as Attendant of the Heir Apparent, could not bear the shame. He quarreled fiercely with Sigu and claimed that Sigu had long borne a grudge against the Xu clan, requesting that the officer responsible for the posthumous name be replaced.

sentences.zh: 太常博士王福畤議曰：「謚者，飾終之稱也，得失一朝，榮辱千載。

translations.literal: Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Wang Fuchou proposed: "A posthumous name is the designation that adorns the end; gain and loss in a single morning, honor and disgrace for a thousand ages."
translations.idiomatic: Erudite Wang Fuchou of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices argued: "A posthumous name is the title that adorns a man's end. What is decided in a single morning may bring honor or disgrace for a thousand years."

sentences.zh: 若使嫌隙是實，即合據法推繩；

translations.literal: "If the grudge is real, then one should follow the law and pursue investigation;
translations.idiomatic: "If the grudge is real, then the law should be invoked and an investigation pursued;

sentences.zh: 如其不虧直道，義不可奪，官不可侵。

translations.literal: if he has not failed the straight Way, righteousness cannot be taken away, and office cannot be encroached upon."
translations.idiomatic: but if he has not failed the straight Way, then righteousness cannot be set aside and his office cannot be infringed."

sentences.zh: 二三其德，何以言禮？

translations.literal: "To be of two or three minds in virtue—how can one speak of ritual?"
translations.idiomatic: "To waver in one's principles—how can one speak of ritual propriety?"

sentences.zh: 福畤忝當官守，匪躬之故。

translations.literal: "Fuchou humbly holds official duty and acts for the sake of not betraying the body."
translations.idiomatic: "I hold this office in humility and act as duty requires, without bending to please others."

sentences.zh: 若順風阿意，背直從曲，更是甲令虛設，將謂禮院無人，何以激揚雅道，顧視同列！

translations.literal: "If one follows the wind and flatters the will, turning the back on the straight and following the crooked, this further makes the statutes an empty show and will make people say the Ritual Office has no men—how then to rouse the refined Way and look one's colleagues in the eye!"
translations.idiomatic: "If I followed the prevailing wind and flattered power, turning my back on what is straight to follow what is crooked, the statutes would become an empty show and people would say the Ritual Office had no men of principle. How then could the refined Way be upheld, or one's colleagues faced with a clear conscience?"

sentences.zh: 請依思古謚議為定。

translations.literal: "I request that Sigu's proposal for the posthumous name be taken as final."
translations.idiomatic: "I ask that Sigu's proposal for the posthumous name be adopted as final."

sentences.zh: 」戶部尚書戴至德謂福畤曰：「高陽公任遇如此，何以定謚為『繆』？

translations.literal: " Minister of Revenue Dai Zhide said to Fuchou: "The Duke of Gaoyang received favor to this degree—how can one fix his posthumous name as Miu?"
translations.idiomatic: " Minister of Revenue Dai Zhide said to Fuchou: "The Duke of Gaoyang enjoyed such favor at court. How can his posthumous name be fixed as Miu?"

sentences.zh: 」答曰：「昔晉司空何曾薨，太常博士秦秀謚為繆丑公。

translations.literal: " He replied: "In former times when Jin Minister of Works He Zeng died, Erudite of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Qin Xiu gave the posthumous name Duke Miu the Ugly."
translations.idiomatic: " He replied: "In former times, when He Zeng, Minister of Works of Jin, died, Erudite Qin Xiu of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices gave him the posthumous name Duke Miu the Ugly."

sentences.zh: 何曾既忠且孝，徒以日食萬錢，所以貶為繆丑。

translations.literal: "He Zeng was both loyal and filial, yet only because he consumed ten thousand coins a day was he demoted to Miu the Ugly."
translations.idiomatic: "He Zeng was loyal and filial in every respect, yet he was demoted to Miu the Ugly solely because he spent ten thousand coins a day on food."

sentences.zh: 況敬宗忠孝不逮於曾，飲食男女之累，有逾於何氏，而謚之為『繆』，無負於許氏矣。

translations.literal: "How much more so Jingzong, whose loyalty and filial piety did not reach Zeng's level, yet whose burdens of food, drink, and women exceeded the He's—to give him the posthumous name Miu does the Xu clan no injustice."
translations.idiomatic: "Jingzong's loyalty and filial piety fell far short of He Zeng's, while his indulgence in food, drink, and women exceeded the He's. To give him the posthumous name Miu does the Xu clan no injustice at all."

sentences.zh: 」時有詔令尚書省五品已上重議，禮部尚書袁思敬議稱：「按謚法『既過能改曰恭』，請謚曰『恭』。

translations.literal: " At the time there was an edict ordering officials of the fifth rank and above in the Department of State Affairs to deliberate again; Minister of Rites Yuan Sijing proposed: "According to the canon of posthumous names, 'having faults yet able to reform is called Gong,' and I request the posthumous name Gong."
translations.idiomatic: " At that time an edict ordered officials of the fifth rank and above in the Department of State Affairs to deliberate again. Minister of Rites Yuan Sijing proposed: "By the canon of posthumous names, 'having faults yet able to reform is called Gong.' I therefore request the posthumous name Gong."

sentences.zh: 」詔從其議。

translations.literal: " An edict followed his proposal.
translations.idiomatic: " An edict adopted his proposal.

sentences.zh: 彥伯，昂之子，起家著作郎。

translations.literal: Yanbo was Ang's son; he began his career as Gentleman of the Writing Office.
translations.idiomatic: Yanbo, Ang's son, began his career as Gentleman of the Writing Office.

sentences.zh: 敬宗末年文筆，多令彥伯代作。

translations.literal: In Jingzong's later years his literary compositions were mostly had Yanbo write in his stead.
translations.idiomatic: In his later years Jingzong had Yanbo write most of his literary compositions for him.

sentences.zh: 又納婢妾讒言，奏流於嶺表，後遇赦得還，除太子舍人。

translations.literal: Again he accepted the slander of maids and concubines, memorialized to exile Yanbo beyond the Lingnan passes; later he met an amnesty and was able to return, and was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: Jingzong again listened to slander from maids and concubines and memorialized to exile Yanbo to the far south. Yanbo was later recalled under an amnesty and appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent.

sentences.zh: 早卒，有集十捲。

translations.literal: He died early; he had a collected writings of ten fascicles.
translations.idiomatic: He died young. His collected writings ran to ten fascicles.

sentences.zh: 李義府

translations.literal: Li Yifu
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu

sentences.zh: 李義府，瀛州饒陽人也。

translations.literal: Li Yifu was a man of Raoyang in Yingzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Li Yifu was a native of Raoyang in Yingzhou.

sentences.zh: 其祖為梓州射洪縣丞，因家於永泰。

translations.literal: His grandfather was assistant magistrate of Shehong county in Zizhou, and the family settled at Yongtai.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather had served as assistant magistrate of Shehong county in Zizhou, and the family thereafter made its home at Yongtai.

sentences.zh: 貞觀八年，劍南道巡察大使李大亮以義府善屬文，表薦之。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Zhenguan, the inspection commissioner of the Jiannan circuit Li Daliang, because Yifu was skilled at literary composition, memorialized to recommend him.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year of the Zhenguan era, Li Daliang, inspection commissioner of the Jiannan circuit, recommended Yifu to the throne because of his skill at literary composition.

sentences.zh: 對策擢第，補門下省典儀。

translations.literal: In the policy-response examination he was advanced to the top grade and appointed Master of Ceremonies in the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He placed at the top of the policy-response examination and was appointed Master of Ceremonies in the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 黃門侍郎劉洎、侍書御史馬周皆稱薦之，尋除監察御史。

translations.literal: Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat Liu Ji and Attendant Censor for Documents Ma Zhou all praised and recommended him; soon he was appointed Investigating Censor.
translations.idiomatic: Liu Ji, Vice Minister of the Palace Secretariat, and Ma Zhou, Attendant Censor for Documents, both praised and recommended him, and he was soon appointed Investigating Censor.

sentences.zh: 又敕義府以本官兼侍晉王。

translations.literal: He was further ordered to serve the Prince of Jin in his original post concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: An edict further ordered him to attend the Prince of Jin while retaining his original post.

sentences.zh: 及升春宮，除太子舍人，加崇賢館直學士，與太子司議郎來濟俱以文翰見知，時稱來、李。

translations.literal: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Yifu was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent and given the additional post of Direct Scholar of the Chongxian Institute; together with the Heir Apparent's Secretariat Drafter Lai Ji he was known for literary composition, and at the time they were called Lai and Li.
translations.idiomatic: When the prince entered the Eastern Palace, Yifu was appointed Attendant of the Heir Apparent and made a Direct Scholar of the Chongxian Institute. He and the Heir Apparent's Secretariat Drafter Lai Ji were both known for their literary gifts, and at court they were spoken of as Lai and Li.

sentences.zh: 義府嘗獻《承華箴》，其辭曰：

translations.literal: Yifu once presented the "Admonition on the Eastern Palace"; its text reads:
translations.idiomatic: Yifu once presented the "Admonition on the Eastern Palace." Its text reads:

sentences.zh: 邃初冥昧，元氣氤氳。

translations.literal: At the remote beginning all was dark and obscure; primordial qi swirled in mist.
translations.idiomatic: In the remote beginning all was dark and obscure, and primordial qi swirled in mist.

sentences.zh: 二儀始闡，三才既分。

translations.literal: The two principles first opened forth, and the three powers were already divided.
translations.idiomatic: The two cosmic principles first unfolded, and heaven, earth, and humanity took their separate forms.

sentences.zh: 司乾立宰，出《震》為君。

translations.literal: He who governs Heaven established the ruler; from the hexagram Zhen came forth the sovereign.
translations.idiomatic: He who governs Heaven established the ruler, and from the hexagram Zhen the sovereign emerged.

sentences.zh: 化昭淳樸，道映典墳。

translations.literal: Transformation made plain the pure and plain; the Way shone upon the canonical texts.
translations.idiomatic: Transformation revealed the pure and plain way of antiquity, and the Way shone upon the canonical texts.

sentences.zh: 功成揖讓，事極華、勳。

translations.literal: When merit was achieved came yielding and abdication; affairs reached their height with Yao and Shun.
translations.idiomatic: When merit was achieved came yielding and abdication, and affairs reached their height with Yao and Shun.

sentences.zh: 肇興夏啟，降及姬文。

translations.literal: It began to rise with Xia Qi and descended to Ji Wen of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: It rose first with Xia Qi and descended to King Wen of Zhou.

sentences.zh: 咸資繼德，永樹高芬。

translations.literal: All relied on inherited virtue and forever planted lofty fragrance.
translations.idiomatic: All relied on inherited virtue and planted a lasting fragrance of renown.

sentences.zh: 百代沿襲，千齡奉聖。

translations.literal: For a hundred generations the pattern was handed down; for a thousand ages the sage was served.
translations.idiomatic: For a hundred generations the pattern was handed down, and for a thousand ages the sage was served.

sentences.zh: 粵若我後，丕承寶命。

translations.literal: Thus our later sovereign greatly received the precious mandate.
translations.idiomatic: Thus our sovereign greatly received the precious mandate of Heaven.

sentences.zh: 允穆三階，爰齊七政。

translations.literal: He harmonized the three ranks and aligned the seven regulators.
translations.idiomatic: He harmonized the three ranks of society and aligned the seven celestial regulators.

sentences.zh: 時雍化洽，風移俗盛。

translations.literal: The age was harmonious and transformation complete; customs shifted and manners flourished.
translations.idiomatic: The age was harmonious and transformation complete; customs shifted and manners flourished.

sentences.zh: 載崇國本，式延家慶。

translations.literal: He exalted the foundation of the state and extended the family's rejoicing.
translations.idiomatic: He exalted the foundation of the state and extended the rejoicing of the imperial house.

sentences.zh: 《震》維標德，《離》警體正。

translations.literal: Zhen marks virtue; Li warns that the person must be upright.
translations.idiomatic: The hexagram Zhen marks virtue; the hexagram Li warns that the person must be upright.

sentences.zh: 寄切宗祧，事隆監撫。

translations.literal: His charge touches closely on the ancestral temple; his affairs are weighty in supervision and nurture.
translations.idiomatic: His charge touches closely on the ancestral temple, and his affairs are weighty in supervision and nurture.

sentences.zh: 思皇茂則，敬詢端輔。

translations.literal: Think deeply on the sovereign's abundant standards; respectfully consult upright assistants.
translations.idiomatic: Think deeply on the sovereign's abundant standards and respectfully consult upright assistants.

sentences.zh: 業光啟、誦，藝優干羽。

translations.literal: His accomplishments shine like Qi and Song; his arts excel like the shield-dance and feather-dance.
translations.idiomatic: His accomplishments shine like the schools of Qi and Song; his arts excel like the shield-dance and feather-dance.

sentences.zh: 九載崇儒，三朝問豎，歷選儲儀，遺文在斯。

translations.literal: For nine years he honored Confucian learning; for three reigns he questioned the young attendants; through successive selections of heir-apparent rites, the legacy texts are here.
translations.idiomatic: For nine years he honored Confucian learning; for three reigns he questioned the young attendants. Through successive selections of heir-apparent rites, the legacy texts stand here.

sentences.zh: 望試登俎，高諭喬枝。

translations.literal: Look to the trial of ascending the sacrificial stand; lofty instruction is like the tall branch.
translations.idiomatic: Look to the trial of ascending the sacrificial stand; lofty instruction is like the tall branch of a tree.

sentences.zh: 俯容思順，非禮無施。

translations.literal: Bow in bearing and think on compliance; what is not ritual do not enact.
translations.idiomatic: Bow in bearing and think on compliance; what is not ritual, do not enact.

sentences.zh: 前修盛業，來哲通規。

translations.literal: The former cultivated their flourishing achievements; later sages grasped the universal rule.
translations.idiomatic: Former worthies cultivated flourishing achievements; later sages grasped the universal rule.

sentences.zh: 飭躬是蹈，則叡問風馳；

translations.literal: If one disciplines the person and treads this path, then sagely inquiry comes like the wind;
translations.idiomatic: If one disciplines the person and treads this path, sagely inquiry comes like the wind;

sentences.zh: 立志或爽，則玄猷日虧。

translations.literal: if one sets the will awry, then the profound design daily declines.
translations.idiomatic: but if one sets the will awry, the profound design daily declines.

sentences.zh: 無恃尊極，修途難測；

translations.literal: Do not rely on supreme eminence; the cultivated path is hard to measure.
translations.idiomatic: Do not rely on supreme eminence, for the cultivated path is hard to measure.

sentences.zh: 無恃親賢，失德靡全。

translations.literal: Do not rely on kin and worthies; lose virtue and nothing remains whole.
translations.idiomatic: Do not rely on kin and worthies; lose virtue and nothing remains whole.

sentences.zh: 勿輕小善，積小而名自聞；

translations.literal: Do not slight small good; accumulate the small and fame will make itself heard.
translations.idiomatic: Do not slight small acts of goodness; accumulate them and fame will make itself heard.

sentences.zh: 勿輕微行，累微而身自正。

translations.literal: Do not slight slight conduct; accumulate the slight and the person will right itself.
translations.idiomatic: Do not slight slight conduct; accumulate it and the person will right itself.

sentences.zh: 佞諛有類，邪巧多方。

translations.literal: Flattery and sycophancy have their kinds; wicked craft has many forms.
translations.idiomatic: Flattery and sycophancy have their kinds, and wicked craft takes many forms.

sentences.zh: 其萌不絕，其害必彰。

translations.literal: If their sprouts are not cut off, their harm will surely be manifest.
translations.idiomatic: If their sprouts are not cut off, their harm will surely be manifest.

sentences.zh: 監言斯屏，儲業攸昌。

translations.literal: Screen off such words of oversight, and the heir's enterprise will flourish.
translations.idiomatic: Screen off such words of oversight, and the heir's enterprise will flourish.

sentences.zh: 竊惟令嗣，有殊前事。

translations.literal: Your servant reflects that the worthy heir differs from former cases.
translations.idiomatic: I reflect that the worthy heir differs from former cases.

sentences.zh: 雖以貴以賢，而非長非次。

translations.literal: Although noble and worthy, he is not the eldest and not in proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Although noble and worthy, he is neither the eldest son nor in proper order of succession.

sentences.zh: 皇明眷德，超倫作貳。

translations.literal: Imperial brightness favors his virtue and sets him above his peers as second.
translations.idiomatic: Imperial brightness favors his virtue and sets him above his peers as heir.

sentences.zh: 匪懋聲華，莫酬恩異。

translations.literal: Unless he makes his reputation flourish, he cannot repay the extraordinary favor.
translations.idiomatic: Unless he makes his reputation flourish, he cannot repay the extraordinary favor shown him.

sentences.zh: 匪崇徽烈，莫符天志。

translations.literal: Unless he exalts his fine achievements, he cannot match Heaven's intent.
translations.idiomatic: Unless he exalts his fine achievements, he cannot match Heaven's intent.

sentences.zh: 勉之又勉，光茲守器。

translations.literal: Exert yourself again and again; make bright this guarding of the vessel.
translations.idiomatic: Exert yourself again and again, and make bright this guarding of the vessel of state.

sentences.zh: 下臣司箴，敢告近侍。

translations.literal: Your lowly servant holds the office of admonition and ventures to inform those close at hand.
translations.idiomatic: Your lowly servant holds the office of admonition and ventures to inform those close at hand.

sentences.zh: 太子表上其文，優詔賜帛四十匹，又令預撰《晉書》。

translations.literal: The crown prince submitted the text in a memorial; an excellent edict granted forty bolts of silk, and he was further ordered to take part in compiling the Book of Jin.
translations.idiomatic: The crown prince submitted the text in a memorial. An edict of praise granted forty bolts of silk, and Yifu was ordered to take part in compiling the Book of Jin.

sentences.zh: 高宗嗣位，遷中書舍人。

translations.literal: When Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Yifu was transferred to Secretariat Drafter.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong succeeded to the throne, Yifu was promoted to Secretariat Drafter.

sentences.zh: 永徽二年，兼修國史，加弘文館學士。

translations.literal: In the second year of Yonghui he concurrently compiled the national history and was given the additional post of Scholar of the Hongwen Institute.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of the Yonghui era he was charged with compiling the national history and made a Scholar of the Hongwen Institute.

sentences.zh: 高宗將立武昭儀為皇后，義府嘗密申協贊，尋擢拜中書侍郎、同中書門下三品，監修國史，賜爵廣平縣男。

translations.literal: Gaozong was about to establish Lady Wu as consort; Yifu had secretly memorialized in support, and soon was promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Third Rank equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery, supervised compilation of the national history, and was granted the title Baron of Guangping county.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Gaozong planned to install Lady Wu as empress, Yifu had secretly memorialized in support. He was soon promoted to Vice Minister of the Secretariat and Third Rank with equal standing in the Secretariat and Chancellery, put in charge of compiling the national history, and enfeoffed as Baron of Guangping.

sentences.zh: 義府貌狀溫恭，與人語必嬉怡微笑，而褊忌陰賊。

translations.literal: Yifu's appearance was mild and respectful; when speaking with people he always smiled pleasantly, yet he was narrow-minded, jealous, and secretly treacherous.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu had a mild and respectful appearance and always smiled pleasantly when he spoke with others, yet he was narrow-minded, jealous, and secretly treacherous.

sentences.zh: 既處權要，欲人附己，微忤意者，輒加傾陷。

translations.literal: Once he occupied a position of power, he wanted people to attach themselves to him; those who slightly offended his will he at once overthrew and entrapped.
translations.idiomatic: Once he held power, he demanded that others attach themselves to him. Anyone who slightly offended him was at once overthrown and entrapped.

sentences.zh: 故時人言義府笑中有刀，又以其柔而害物，亦謂之「李貓。

translations.literal: Therefore people of the time said Yifu had a knife within his smile; also because he was soft yet harmed things, they also called him "Li the Cat."
translations.idiomatic: People of the time therefore said that Yifu had a knife within his smile, and because he was soft yet harmed others, they also called him "Li the Cat."

sentences.zh: 」顯慶元年，以本官兼太子右庶子，進爵為侯。

translations.literal: " In the first year of Xianqing he held his original post concurrently as Right Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent and was advanced in rank to Marquis.
translations.idiomatic: " In the first year of the Xianqing era he was made Right Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent while retaining his original post, and was advanced in rank to Marquis.

sentences.zh: 有洛州婦人淳于氏，坐奸繫於大理，義府聞其姿色，囑大理丞畢正義求為別宅婦，特為雪其罪。

translations.literal: There was a woman of Luozhou, the Chunyu clan, imprisoned in the Court of Judicial Review on a charge of adultery. Yifu heard of her beauty and instructed Vice Director of the Court Bi Zhengyi to seek her as a woman for his separate residence, and specially cleared her crime.
translations.idiomatic: A woman of the Chunyu clan in Luozhou was imprisoned in the Court of Judicial Review on a charge of adultery. When Yifu heard of her beauty, he instructed Vice Director Bi Zhengyi to obtain her for his separate residence and had her crime cleared.

sentences.zh: 卿段寶玄疑其故，遽以狀聞，詔令按其事，正義惶懼自縊而死。

translations.literal: Senior Director Duan Baoxuan suspected the reason and hastily reported the matter; an edict ordered investigation of the affair, and Zhengyi in fear and panic hanged himself to death.
translations.idiomatic: Senior Director Duan Baoxuan suspected what was happening and hastily reported the matter. An edict ordered an investigation, and Zhengyi, in fear and panic, hanged himself.

sentences.zh: 侍御史王義方廷奏義府犯狀，因言其初容貌為劉洎、馬周所幸，由此得進，言詞猥褻。

translations.literal: Attendant Censor Wang Yifang memorialized in court on Yifu's offenses, and further said that at first his appearance had been favored by Liu Ji and Ma Zhou, and through this he had advanced; his words were obscene and lewd.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Censor Wang Yifang memorialized in court on Yifu's offenses and said that at first his appearance had won the favor of Liu Ji and Ma Zhou, through which he had advanced. His language was obscene and lewd.

sentences.zh: 帝怒，出義方為萊州司戶，而不問義府奸濫之罪。

translations.literal: The emperor was angry and sent Yifang out as revenue clerk of Laizhou, but did not inquire into Yifu's crimes of wickedness and excess.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was angry and sent Yifang out as revenue clerk of Laizhou, but did not inquire into Yifu's crimes of wickedness and excess.

sentences.zh: 義府云：「王御史妄相彈奏，得無愧乎？

translations.literal: Yifu said: "Censor Wang recklessly impeached me—should he not feel shame?"
translations.idiomatic: Yifu said: "Censor Wang recklessly impeached me. Should he not feel ashamed?"

sentences.zh: 」義方對云：「仲尼為魯司寇七日，誅少正卯於兩觀之下；

translations.literal: " Yifang replied: "Confucius as Minister of Crime of Lu for seven days executed Shaozheng Mao beneath the two towers;"
translations.idiomatic: " Yifang replied: "Confucius served as Minister of Crime of Lu for seven days and executed Shaozheng Mao beneath the two towers of the gate."

sentences.zh: 義方任御史旬有六日，不能去奸邪於雙闕之前，實以為愧。

translations.literal: Yifang served as censor for sixteen days and could not remove the wicked and treacherous before the paired towers—he truly feels shame.
translations.idiomatic: I have served as censor for sixteen days and could not remove the wicked and treacherous before the paired towers of the palace gate. That is what truly shames me."

sentences.zh: 」尋兼太子左庶子。

translations.literal: " Soon he was given the concurrent post of Left Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent.
translations.idiomatic: " He was soon made Left Vice Grand Tutor of the Heir Apparent as well.

sentences.zh: 二年，代崔敦禮為中書令，兼檢校御史大夫，監修國史、學士並如故。

translations.literal: In the second year he replaced Cui Dunli as Chief Secretariat Counselor, concurrently acting as Censor-in-Chief, and supervised compilation of the national history and held his scholar post as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he replaced Cui Dunli as Chief Secretariat Counselor, was given acting authority as Censor-in-Chief, and continued as before to supervise compilation of the national history and hold his scholar post.

sentences.zh: 尋加太子賓客，進封河間郡公。

translations.literal: Soon he was given the additional post of Guest of the Heir Apparent and advanced to Duke of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: He was soon made Guest of the Heir Apparent and advanced to Duke of Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 三年，又追贈其父德晟為魏州刺史，諸子孩抱者並列清官，詔為造甲第，榮寵莫之能比。

translations.literal: In the third year his father Desheng was posthumously given the post of prefect of Weizhou; all his sons still in infancy were listed among pure offices; an edict ordered construction of a grand mansion for him—honor and favor none could match.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year his father Desheng was posthumously appointed prefect of Weizhou. All his sons still in infancy were given pure offices, and an edict ordered a grand mansion built for him. No one at court enjoyed honor and favor to match his.

sentences.zh: 而義府貪冒無厭，與母、妻及諸子、女婿賣官鬻獄，其門如市。

translations.literal: Yet Yifu was greedy and reckless without satiety; with his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law he sold offices and traded in judicial cases, and his gate was like a market.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Yifu was insatiably greedy. With his mother, wife, sons, and sons-in-law he sold offices and traded in judicial cases, and his gate was thronged like a market.

sentences.zh: 多引腹心，廣樹朋黨，傾動朝野。

translations.literal: He drew in many trusted intimates, broadly planted factional cliques, and swayed court and countryside.
translations.idiomatic: He drew in many trusted intimates, built broad networks of faction, and swayed court and countryside alike.

sentences.zh: 初，杜正倫為中書侍郎，義府時任典儀，至是乃與正倫同為中書令。

translations.literal: At first Du Zhenglun was Vice Minister of the Secretariat while Yifu then held the post of Master of Ceremonies; now the two of them were both Chief Secretariat Counselor.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Du Zhenglun had been Vice Minister of the Secretariat while Yifu held the post of Master of Ceremonies. Now the two men served together as Chief Secretariat Counselor.

sentences.zh: 正倫每以先進自處，不下義府，而中書侍郎李友益密與正倫共圖議義府，更相伺察。

translations.literal: Zhenglun always placed himself as senior and would not defer to Yifu, while Vice Minister Li Youyi secretly joined Zhenglun in plotting against Yifu, each watching the other.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun always treated himself as the senior man and would not defer to Yifu. Vice Minister Li Youyi secretly joined Zhenglun in plotting against Yifu, and the two men watched each other closely.

sentences.zh: 義府知而密令人封奏其事。

translations.literal: Yifu learned of it and secretly had someone seal and memorialize the matter.
translations.idiomatic: When Yifu learned of this, he secretly had someone seal and memorialize the matter to the throne.

sentences.zh: 正倫與義府訟於上前，各有曲直。

translations.literal: Zhenglun and Yifu argued their case before the emperor; each had right and wrong.
translations.idiomatic: Zhenglun and Yifu argued their case before the emperor, and each had some right and some wrong on his side.

sentences.zh: 上以大臣不和，兩責之，左貶義府為普州刺史，正倫為橫州刺史，友益配流峰州。

translations.literal: The emperor, because the great ministers were not harmonious, blamed both of them and demoted Yifu to prefect of Puzhou and Zhenglun to prefect of Hengzhou; Youyi was sentenced to exile at Fengzhou.
translations.idiomatic: Because the great ministers were at odds, the emperor blamed both men and demoted Yifu to prefect of Puzhou and Zhenglun to prefect of Hengzhou. Youyi was sentenced to exile at Fengzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年，復召義府兼吏部尚書、同中書門下三品，自余官封如故。

translations.literal: In the fourth year Yifu was again summoned and made Minister of the Civil Service concurrently, Third Rank equal to the Secretariat and Chancellery; his other offices and enfeoffment remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year Yifu was recalled and made Minister of the Civil Service with Third Rank equal standing in the Secretariat and Chancellery. His other offices and enfeoffment remained unchanged.

sentences.zh: 龍朔元年，丁母憂去職。

translations.literal: In the first year of Longshuo he left office on mourning for his mother.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Longshuo era he left office to observe mourning for his mother.

sentences.zh: 二年，起復為司列太常伯、同東西台三品。

translations.literal: In the second year he was recalled from mourning as Minister of Rites in charge of ranks and Third Rank equal to the Eastern and Western Offices.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year he was recalled from mourning as Minister of Rites in charge of ranks and Third Rank with equal standing on the Eastern and Western Offices.

sentences.zh: 義府尋請改葬其祖父，營墓於永康陵側。

translations.literal: Yifu soon requested to rebury his grandfather and built a tomb beside Yongkang Mausoleum.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu soon requested permission to rebury his grandfather and built a tomb beside Yongkang Mausoleum.

sentences.zh: 三原令李孝節私課丁夫車牛，為其載土築墳，晝夜不息。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Sanyuan Li Xiaojie privately levied corvée laborers, carts, and oxen to haul earth and build the mound for him, day and night without cease.
translations.idiomatic: Li Xiaojie, magistrate of Sanyuan, privately levied corvée laborers, carts, and oxen to haul earth and build the mound for him, working day and night without cease.

sentences.zh: 於是高陵、櫟陽、富平、雲陽、華原、同官、涇陽等七縣，以孝節之故，懼不得已，悉課丁車赴役。

translations.literal: Thereupon the seven counties of Gaoling, Liyang, Fuping, Yunyang, Huayuan, Tongguan, and Jingyang, because of Xiaojie, in fear had no choice and all levied corvée laborers and carts for the service.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon the seven counties of Gaoling, Liyang, Fuping, Yunyang, Huayuan, Tongguan, and Jingyang, fearing Xiaojie's power, had no choice but to levy corvée laborers and carts for the work.

sentences.zh: 高陵令張敬業恭勤怯懦，不堪其勞，死於作所。

translations.literal: The magistrate of Gaoling Zhang Jingye was respectful, diligent, timid, and weak; he could not bear the labor and died at the work site.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Jingye, magistrate of Gaoling, was respectful and diligent but timid and frail. He could not bear the labor and died at the work site.

sentences.zh: 王公已下，爭致贈遺，其羽儀、導從、轜輶、器服，並窮極奢侈。

translations.literal: From princes and dukes downward, all vied to send gifts; his escort, attendants, carriages, and vessels and garments were all pushed to the utmost luxury.
translations.idiomatic: From princes and dukes downward, all vied to send gifts. His escort, attendants, carriages, and vessels and garments were pushed to the utmost luxury.

sentences.zh: 又會葬車馬祖奠供帳，自灞橋屬於三原，七十里間，相繼不絕。

translations.literal: Again at the joint burial the carriages, horses, offerings at the roadside, and supply tents from Ba Bridge extending to Sanyuan—for seventy li they followed one after another without break.
translations.idiomatic: At the joint burial the carriages, horses, roadside offerings, and supply tents stretched from Ba Bridge to Sanyuan, and for seventy li they followed one after another without a break.

sentences.zh: 武德已來，王公葬送之盛，未始有也。

translations.literal: Since Wude there had never been such magnificence in the burial send-off of princes and dukes.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Wude era there had never been such magnificence in the burial procession of a prince or duke.

sentences.zh: 義府本無藻鑑才，怙武後之勢，專以賣官為事。

translations.literal: Yifu originally had no talent for discerning men; relying on Empress Wu's power, he devoted himself solely to selling offices.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu had no real talent for judging men. Relying on Empress Wu's power, he devoted himself solely to selling offices.

sentences.zh: 銓序失次，人多怨讟。

translations.literal: The order of selection and ranking was lost, and many people murmured in resentment.
translations.idiomatic: The order of selection and ranking was thrown into chaos, and resentment spread widely.

sentences.zh: 時殷王初出閣，又以義府兼王府長史。

translations.literal: At the time the Prince of Yin had just left the palace quarters, and Yifu was again made Chief Secretary of the princely establishment concurrently.
translations.idiomatic: At that time the Prince of Yin had just left the palace quarters, and Yifu was again made Chief Secretary of the princely establishment.

sentences.zh: 三年，遷右相，殷王府長史仍知選事並如故。

translations.literal: In the third year he was transferred to Right Chancellor; his post as Chief Secretary of the Prince of Yin's establishment and his charge of selection affairs remained as before.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year he was transferred to Right Chancellor while continuing as Chief Secretary of the Prince of Yin's establishment and retaining charge of selection affairs.

sentences.zh: 義府入則諂言自媚，出則肆其奸宄，百僚畏之，無敢言其過者。

translations.literal: Yifu within the palace spoke flattering words to please himself; outside he unleashed his treachery and wickedness. The hundred officials feared him, and none dared speak of his faults.
translations.idiomatic: Within the palace Yifu spoke flattering words to please those in power; outside it he unleashed his treachery and wickedness. The officials feared him, and none dared speak of his faults.

sentences.zh: 帝頗知其罪失，從容誡義府云：「聞卿兒子、女婿皆不謹慎，多作罪過，我亦為卿掩覆，未即公言，卿可誡勖，勿令如此。

translations.literal: The emperor quite knew his crimes and faults, and calmly admonished Yifu: "I hear that your sons and sons-in-law are all careless and commit many offenses. I have also covered this for you and have not yet spoken of it publicly. You may warn and encourage them—do not let it be thus."
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was well aware of his crimes and faults and calmly admonished him: "I hear that your sons and sons-in-law are all careless and commit many offenses. I have covered this for you and have not yet spoken of it publicly. Warn and encourage them. Do not let things go on this way."

sentences.zh: 」義府勃然變色，腮頸俱起，徐曰：「誰向陛下道此？

translations.literal: " Yifu suddenly changed color in anger; his cheeks and neck both swelled, and he said slowly: "Who told Your Majesty this?"
translations.idiomatic: " Yifu flushed with anger, his cheeks and neck swelling, and said slowly: "Who told Your Majesty this?"

sentences.zh: 」上曰：「但我言如是，何須問我所從得耶！

translations.literal: " The emperor said: "It is simply that I speak thus—why must you ask where I learned it!"
translations.idiomatic: " The emperor said: "It is simply that I speak thus. Why must you ask where I learned it?"

sentences.zh: 」義府睆然，殊不引咎，緩步而去。

translations.literal: " Yifu stared blankly, showed no sign of accepting blame whatsoever, and walked away with slow steps.
translations.idiomatic: " Yifu stared blankly, showed no sign of accepting blame, and walked away with slow steps.

sentences.zh: 上亦優容之。

translations.literal: The emperor also treated him with forbearance.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor treated him with forbearance nonetheless.

sentences.zh: 初，五禮儀注，自前代相沿，吉凶畢舉。

translations.literal: At first the annotated rituals of the Five Rites, handed down from former ages, included both auspicious and inauspicious rites in full.
translations.idiomatic: At first the annotated rituals of the Five Rites, handed down from former ages, included both auspicious and inauspicious rites in full.

sentences.zh: 太常博士蕭楚材、孔志約以皇室凶禮為預備凶事，非臣子所宜言之。

translations.literal: Erudites of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Xiao Chucai and Kong Zhiyue held that inauspicious rites of the imperial house were preparations for inauspicious events, and were not what subjects should speak of.
translations.idiomatic: Erudites Xiao Chucai and Kong Zhiyue of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices argued that inauspicious rites of the imperial house were preparations for inauspicious events and were not what subjects should speak of.

sentences.zh: 義府深然之。

translations.literal: Yifu deeply agreed with this.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu strongly agreed.

sentences.zh: 於是悉刪而焚焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon he deleted them all and burned them.
translations.idiomatic: He then deleted them all and had them burned.

sentences.zh: 義府既貴之後，又自言本出趙郡，始與諸李敘昭穆，而無賴之徒苟合，藉其權勢，拜伏為兄叔者甚眾。

translations.literal: After Yifu had become noble, he also declared of himself that he originally came from Zhao commandery and began to arrange senior and junior kinship with the various Lis; worthless fellows who joined him opportunistically, borrowing his power, were very many in bowing and calling him elder brother or uncle.
translations.idiomatic: After Yifu had risen to power, he declared that his family originally came from Zhao commandery and began to arrange senior and junior kinship with the various Li clans. Worthless men who joined him opportunistically, borrowing his power, were very many in bowing to him as elder brother or uncle.

sentences.zh: 給事中李崇德初亦與同譜敘昭穆，及義府出為普州刺史，遂即除削。

translations.literal: Attendant Within the Gates Li Chongde at first also arranged senior and junior kinship in the same genealogy; when Yifu went out as prefect of Puzhou, he was at once struck from the rolls.
translations.idiomatic: Attendant Within the Gates Li Chongde had at first also arranged senior and junior kinship with Yifu in the same genealogy. When Yifu was sent out as prefect of Puzhou, Chongde was at once struck from the rolls.

sentences.zh: 義府聞而銜之，及重為宰相，乃令人誣構其罪，竟下獄自殺。

translations.literal: Yifu heard of it and bore a grudge; when he again became chief minister, he had someone falsely charge him with crimes, and in the end Chongde was put in prison and killed himself.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu heard of this and bore a deep grudge. When he again became chief minister, he had someone fabricate charges against Chongde, who was eventually imprisoned and took his own life.

sentences.zh: 初，貞觀中，太宗命吏部尚書高士廉、御史大夫韋挺、中書侍郎岑文本、禮部侍郎令狐德棻等及四方士大夫諳練門閥者修《氏族志》，勒成百卷，升降去取，時稱允當，頒下諸州，藏為永式。

translations.literal: At first, in Zhenguan, Taizong ordered Minister of the Civil Service Gao Shilian, Censor-in-Chief Wei Ting, Vice Minister of the Secretariat Cen Wende, Vice Minister of Rites Linghu Defen, and others, together with scholar-officials from all directions skilled in lineage and gates, to compile the Genealogies of Clans, which was completed in a hundred fascicles. The promotions and demotions in selection were at the time called fair, distributed to all prefectures, and stored as a permanent standard.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the Zhenguan era, Emperor Taizong ordered Gao Shilian, Minister of the Civil Service, Wei Ting, Censor-in-Chief, Cen Wende, Vice Minister of the Secretariat, Linghu Defen, Vice Minister of Rites, and other scholar-officials from across the realm skilled in lineage and family standing to compile the Genealogies of Clans. The work ran to a hundred fascicles. Its promotions and demotions were widely judged fair, distributed to every prefecture, and preserved as a permanent standard.

sentences.zh: 義府恥其家代無名，乃奏改此書，專委禮部郎中孔志約、著作郎楊仁卿、太子洗馬史玄道、太常丞呂才重修。

translations.literal: Yifu was ashamed that his family for generations had no fame, and therefore memorialized to revise this book, specially entrusting Section Director of Rites Kong Zhiyue, Gentleman of the Writing Office Yang Renqing, Groom of the Heir Apparent Shi Xuandao, and Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Lü Cai to revise it anew.
translations.idiomatic: Ashamed that his family had no distinguished name for generations, Yifu memorialized to revise the book and entrusted the work solely to Kong Zhiyue, Section Director of Rites, Yang Renqing, Gentleman of the Writing Office, Shi Xuandao, Groom of the Heir Apparent, and Lü Cai, Vice Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 志約等遂立格云：「皇朝得五品官者，皆升士流。

translations.literal: Zhiyue and the others thereupon established a rule saying: "In our dynasty all who obtain office of the fifth rank are promoted into the gentry stream."
translations.idiomatic: Zhiyue and the others thereupon established a rule stating: "In our dynasty all who obtain office of the fifth rank are to be entered into the gentry stream."

sentences.zh: 」於是兵卒以軍功致五品者，盡入書限，更名為《姓氏錄》。

translations.literal: " Thereupon soldiers and common troops who through military merit reached the fifth rank all entered the limits of the book, and it was renamed the Record of Surnames.
translations.idiomatic: " Thereupon soldiers who through military merit reached the fifth rank all entered the book's limits, and it was renamed the Record of Surnames.

sentences.zh: 由是搢紳士大夫多恥被甄敘，皆號此書為「勳格」。

translations.literal: Because of this many gentry scholar-officials were ashamed to be entered in selection and all called this book the "Merit Register."
translations.idiomatic: Because of this many gentry scholar-officials were ashamed to be entered in the register, and all called the book the "Merit Register."

sentences.zh: 義府仍奏收天下《氏族志》本焚之。

translations.literal: Yifu still memorialized to collect all copies of the Genealogies of Clans throughout the realm and burn them.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu also memorialized to collect every copy of the Genealogies of Clans in the realm and have them burned.

sentences.zh: 關東魏、齊舊姓，雖皆淪替，猶相矜尚，自為婚姻。

translations.literal: The old surnames of Wei and Qi east of the Pass, although all had fallen into decline, still prized and honored one another and made marriages among themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The old surnames of Wei and Qi east of the Pass, though all had fallen into decline, still prized one another and made marriages only among themselves.

sentences.zh: 義府為子求婚不得，乃奏隴西李等七家，不得相與為婚。

translations.literal: Yifu, because he could not obtain a marriage alliance for his son, memorialized that the seven families including the Li of Longxi might not marry with one another.
translations.idiomatic: When Yifu failed to obtain a marriage alliance for his son, he memorialized that the seven great families, including the Li of Longxi, might not intermarry with one another.

sentences.zh: 陰陽占候人杜元紀為義府望氣，雲「所居宅有獄氣，發積錢二千萬乃可厭勝。

translations.literal: The yin-yang diviner Du Yuanji performed qi-watching for Yifu and said: "The residence you dwell in has the qi of prison; you must disburse twenty million in stored cash before it can be overcome."
translations.idiomatic: The yin-yang diviner Du Yuanji performed qi-watching for Yifu and said: "Your residence bears the qi of prison. You must disburse twenty million in stored cash before the omen can be overcome."

sentences.zh: 」義府信之，聚斂更急切。

translations.literal: " Yifu believed him and gathered wealth even more urgently.
translations.idiomatic: " Yifu believed him and gathered wealth even more urgently.

sentences.zh: 義府居母服，有制朔望給哭假，義府輒微服與元紀凌晨共出城東，登古冢候望，哀禮都廢。

translations.literal: Yifu was in mourning for his mother; there was a statute giving leave for lamentation on the first and fifteenth of the month, yet Yifu would put on ordinary dress and with Yuanji at dawn together go out east of the city, climb an ancient mound to observe the heavens, and abandon mourning rites entirely.
translations.idiomatic: While Yifu was in mourning for his mother, regulations allowed leave for lamentation on the first and fifteenth of each month. Yet he would put on ordinary dress and at dawn go out east of the city with Yuanji to climb an ancient mound and observe the heavens, abandoning mourning rites entirely.

sentences.zh: 由是人皆言其窺覘災眚，陰懷異圖。

translations.literal: Because of this everyone said he was spying on calamities and portents and secretly harbored a different design.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this everyone said he was spying on calamities and portents and secretly harbored treasonous designs.

sentences.zh: 義府又遣其子右司議郎津，召長孫無忌之孫延，謂曰：「相為得一官，數日詔書當出。

translations.literal: Yifu also sent his son, Right Secretariat Drafter of the Heir Apparent Jin, to summon Zhangsun Wuji's grandson Yan and say to him: "I can get you an office; in a few days the edict will issue."
translations.idiomatic: Yifu also sent his son Jin, Right Secretariat Drafter of the Heir Apparent, to summon Zhangsun Wuji's grandson Yan and tell him: "I can get you an office. The edict will issue in a few days."

sentences.zh: 」居五日，果授延司津監，乃取延錢七百貫。
