translations.literal: " After five days Yan was indeed appointed Director of the Office of River Transport, and Jin then took seven hundred strings of cash from Yan.
translations.idiomatic: " Five days later Yan was indeed appointed Director of the Office of River Transport, and Jin then took seven hundred strings of cash from him.

sentences.zh: 於是右金吾倉曹參軍楊行穎表言義府罪狀，制下司刑太常伯劉祥道與侍御詳刑對推其事，仍令司空李勣監焉。

translations.literal: Thereupon Right Golden Guard Army Revenue Clerk Yang Xingying memorialized on Yifu's crimes; an edict ordered Minister of Punishments Liu Xiangdao and the Attendant Censor for Detailed Punishment jointly to investigate the matter, and still ordered Minister of Works Li Ji to supervise it.
translations.idiomatic: Thereupon Yang Xingying, Right Golden Guard Army Revenue Clerk, memorialized on Yifu's crimes. An edict ordered Liu Xiangdao, Minister of Punishments, and the Attendant Censor for Detailed Punishment jointly to investigate the case, with Minister of Works Li Ji appointed to supervise.

sentences.zh: 按皆有實，乃下制曰：「右相、行殷王府長史、河間郡公李義府，洩禁中之語，鬻寵授之朝恩；

translations.literal: The investigation found everything substantiated, and an edict was issued saying: "Right Chancellor, acting Chief Secretary of the Prince of Yin's establishment, Duke of Hejian commandery Li Yifu leaked words from within the forbidden precinct, sold favor and traded in court grace;
translations.idiomatic: The investigation substantiated every charge, and an edict was issued: "Right Chancellor, acting Chief Secretary of the Prince of Yin's establishment, Duke of Hejian commandery Li Yifu leaked words from within the forbidden precinct and sold favor in exchange for court grace;

sentences.zh: 交占候之人，輕朔望之哀禮。

translations.literal: associated with diviners of portents, and treated lightly the mourning rites of the first and fifteenth;
translations.idiomatic: associated with diviners of portents and treated lightly the mourning rites due on the first and fifteenth of the month;

sentences.zh: 蓄邪黷貨，實玷衣冠；

translations.literal: hoarded wickedness and amassed goods, truly staining the robes and caps;
translations.idiomatic: hoarded wickedness and amassed illicit goods, truly staining the robes and caps of office;

sentences.zh: 稔惡嫉賢，載虧政道。

translations.literal: ripened in evil and envied the worthy, repeatedly harming the way of government.
translations.idiomatic: ripened in evil and envied the worthy, repeatedly harming the way of government.

sentences.zh: 特以任使多年，未忍便加重罰，宜從遐棄，以肅朝倫。

translations.literal: Only because he has been employed for many years, we cannot bear to impose heavy punishment at once; he should be cast to a distant place to rectify court order.
translations.idiomatic: Only because he has served for many years can we not bear to impose heavy punishment at once. He should be cast to a distant place to restore order at court.

sentences.zh: 可除名長流巂州。

translations.literal: His name may be struck from the rolls and he long exiled to Xizhou.
translations.idiomatic: His name is to be struck from the rolls and he is long exiled to Xizhou.

sentences.zh: 其子太子右司議郎津，專恃權門，罕懷忌憚，姦淫是務，賄賂無厭，交遊非所，潛報機密，亦宜明罰，屏跡荒裔。

translations.literal: His son, Right Secretariat Drafter of the Heir Apparent Jin, relied solely on the gate of power, rarely harbored fear, made lewdness his pursuit, was insatiable in bribes, associated with improper persons, and secretly reported confidential matters; he too should receive clear punishment and be banished to the wild borderlands.
translations.idiomatic: His son Jin, Right Secretariat Drafter of the Heir Apparent, relied solely on his father's power, rarely showed fear, pursued lewdness, was insatiable in bribes, associated with improper persons, and secretly reported confidential matters. He too should receive clear punishment and be banished to the wild borderlands.

sentences.zh: 可除名長流振州。

translations.literal: His name may be struck from the rolls and he long exiled to Zhenzhou.
translations.idiomatic: His name is to be struck from the rolls and he is long exiled to Zhenzhou.

sentences.zh: 」義府次子率府長史洽、千牛備身洋、子婿少府主簿柳元貞等，皆憑恃受贓，併除名長流延州。

translations.literal: " Yifu's second son, Chief Secretary of the Palace Guard Office Xia, Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant Yang, and son-in-law Assistant Magistrate of the Palace Workshop Liu Yuanzhen and others all relied on his power to accept bribes; together their names were struck from the rolls and they were long exiled to Yanzhou.
translations.idiomatic: " Yifu's second son Xia, Chief Secretary of the Palace Guard Office, his son Yang, Thousand-Ox Guard Attendant, and his son-in-law Liu Yuanzhen, Assistant Magistrate of the Palace Workshop, and others all relied on his power to accept bribes. Together their names were struck from the rolls and they were long exiled to Yanzhou.

sentences.zh: 朝野莫不稱慶，時人為之語曰：「今日巨唐年，還誅四凶族。

translations.literal: " Court and countryside all celebrated, and people of the time made a saying: "In this great Tang year, the four wicked clans are again put to death."
translations.idiomatic: " Court and countryside alike celebrated, and people of the time made a saying: "In this great Tang year, the four wicked clans are put to death once again."

sentences.zh: 」四凶者，謂洽及柳元貞等四人也。

translations.literal: " The four wicked ones meant Xia and Liu Yuanzhen and the other four men.
translations.idiomatic: " The four wicked ones referred to Xia, Liu Yuanzhen, and four others.

sentences.zh: 或作《河間道行軍元帥劉祥道破銅山大賊李義府露布》，榜之通衢。

translations.literal: Some composed a battle report titled "Marshal Liu Xiangdao of the Hejian Route Army Crushes the Great Bandit Li Yifu of Copper Mountain" and posted it at the crossroads.
translations.idiomatic: Someone composed a battle report titled "Marshal Liu Xiangdao of the Hejian Route Army Crushes the Great Bandit Li Yifu of Copper Mountain" and posted it at the crossroads.

sentences.zh: 義府先多取人奴婢，及敗，一時奔散，各歸其家。

translations.literal: Yifu had earlier taken many people's male and female slaves; when he fell, they all at once fled and scattered, each returning to his own household.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu had earlier taken many people's slaves. When he fell, they all fled at once and scattered, each returning to his own household.

sentences.zh: 《露布》稱「混奴婢而亂放，各識家而競入」者，謂此也。

translations.literal: The battle report's phrase "mixing male and female slaves and releasing them in disorder, each recognizing his household and racing to enter" referred to this.
translations.idiomatic: The battle report's phrase about "mixing male and female slaves and releasing them in disorder, each recognizing his household and racing home" referred to this.

sentences.zh: 乾封元年，大赦，長流人不許還，義府憂憤發疾卒，年五十餘。

translations.literal: In the first year of Qianfeng there was a great amnesty, but long exiles were not permitted to return. Yifu in grief and anger fell ill and died, aged more than fifty.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of the Qianfeng era a great amnesty was proclaimed, but long exiles were not permitted to return. Yifu fell ill from grief and anger and died, aged more than fifty.

sentences.zh: 文集三十捲，傳於代；

translations.literal: His collected writings were thirty fascicles, transmitted in his age;
translations.idiomatic: His collected writings ran to thirty fascicles and were transmitted in his age;

sentences.zh: 又著《宦遊記》二十捲，尋亡失。

translations.literal: he also wrote the Records of Official Travel in twenty fascicles, which soon were lost.
translations.idiomatic: he also wrote the Records of Official Travel in twenty fascicles, which were soon lost.

sentences.zh: 自義府流放後，朝士常憂懼，恐其復來，及聞其死，於是始安。

translations.literal: From the time Yifu was exiled, court gentlemen were constantly anxious and fearful lest he return; when they heard of his death, only then did they grow calm.
translations.idiomatic: After Yifu was exiled, court gentlemen lived in constant anxiety, fearing he might return. Only when they heard of his death did they at last feel calm.

sentences.zh: 少子湛

translations.literal: The younger son Zhan
translations.idiomatic: The Younger Son Zhan

sentences.zh: 義府少子湛，年六歲時，以父貴授周王文學。

translations.literal: Yifu's younger son Zhan, when six years old, because of his father's nobility was appointed Literary Scholar of the Prince of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: Yifu's younger son Zhan, at the age of six, was appointed Literary Scholar of the Prince of Zhou because of his father's rank.

sentences.zh: 神龍初，累遷右散騎常侍，襲封河間郡公。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong he was repeatedly promoted to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry, and inherited enfeoffment as Duke of Hejian commandery.
translations.idiomatic: Early in the Shenlong era he rose through successive posts to Right Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and inherited the enfeoffment as Duke of Hejian commandery.

sentences.zh: 時鳳閣侍郎張柬之將誅張易之兄弟，遂引湛為左羽林將軍，令與敬暉等啟請皇太子，備陳將誅易之兄弟意，太子許之。

translations.literal: At the time Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion Zhang Jianzhi was about to execute Zhang Yizhi and his brothers, and therefore brought in Zhan as General of the Left Forest of Feathers, ordering him together with Jing Hui and others to memorialize requesting the crown prince and fully stating the intent to execute the Yizhi brothers; the crown prince assented.
translations.idiomatic: At that time Zhang Jianzhi, Vice Minister of the Phoenix Pavilion, was planning to execute Zhang Yizhi and his brothers. He brought in Zhan as General of the Left Forest of Feathers and ordered him, together with Jing Hui and others, to petition the crown prince and explain fully their plan to kill the Yizhi brothers. The crown prince assented.

sentences.zh: 及兵發，湛與右羽林大將軍李多祚等詣東宮迎皇太子，拒而不時出，湛進啟曰：「逆豎反道亂常，將圖不軌，宗社危敗，實在須臾。

translations.literal: When the troops set out, Zhan together with Right General of the Forest of Feathers Li Duozuo and others went to the Eastern Palace to welcome the crown prince, who refused and did not come out in time. Zhan advanced and memorialized: "The rebellious villains violate the Way and disorder the norm, plotting unorthodox designs; the altars of state are in peril of ruin, and it is truly a matter of moments."
translations.idiomatic: When the troops set out, Zhan went with Li Duozuo, Right General of the Forest of Feathers, and others to the Eastern Palace to welcome the crown prince, who refused to come out promptly. Zhan stepped forward and said: "The rebellious villains violate the Way and disorder the norm and plot treason. The altars of state stand on the brink of ruin, and the danger is truly a matter of moments."

sentences.zh: 湛等諸將與南衙執事剋期誅翦，伏願殿下暫至玄武門，以副眾望。

translations.literal: Zhan and the other generals together with the duty officers of the Southern Yamen have set a date to cut down and destroy them; we humbly wish Your Highness for a time to come to the Xuanwu Gate to answer the hopes of the multitude.
translations.idiomatic: We generals, together with the duty officers of the Southern Yamen, have set a date to cut them down. We humbly beg Your Highness to come for a time to the Xuanwu Gate and answer the hopes of all.

sentences.zh: 」太子曰：「凶豎悖亂，誠合誅夷，然聖躬不豫，慮有驚動。

translations.literal: " The crown prince said: "The wicked villains are rebellious and disorderly and truly ought to be executed and exterminated, yet the sacred person is unwell, and I fear there may be disturbance."
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince said: "The wicked villains are rebellious and truly ought to be executed, yet the sacred person is unwell, and I fear there may be disturbance."

sentences.zh: 公等且止，以俟後圖。

translations.literal: You gentlemen for now stop and wait for a later plan."
translations.idiomatic: You gentlemen must stop for now and wait for a later plan."

sentences.zh: 」湛曰：「諸將棄家族，共宰相同心戮力，匡輔社稷，殿下奈何不哀其懇誠而欲陷之鼎鑊？

translations.literal: " Zhan said: "The generals have abandoned their clans and families and together with the chief minister with one heart exert their strength to support the altars of state—why does Your Highness not pity their earnest sincerity and instead wish to cast them into the cauldron?"
translations.idiomatic: " Zhan said: "We generals have abandoned our families and, together with the chief minister, exert our strength with one heart to support the altars of state. Why does Your Highness not pity our earnest sincerity and instead wish to cast us into the cauldron?"

sentences.zh: 湛等微命，雖不足惜，殿下速出自止遏。

translations.literal: Zhan and the others' slight lives, though not worth cherishing—Your Highness, quickly come forth yourself to stop and restrain them."
translations.idiomatic: Our slight lives are not worth cherishing, but Your Highness must quickly come forth yourself to stop and restrain the plot."

sentences.zh: 」太子乃馳馬就路。

translations.literal: " The crown prince thereupon spurred his horse onto the road.
translations.idiomatic: " The crown prince thereupon spurred his horse onto the road.

sentences.zh: 湛從至玄武門，斬關而入，率所部兵直至則天所寢長生殿，環繞侍衛。

translations.literal: Zhan followed to the Xuanwu Gate, cut through the barrier and entered, led his unit of troops straight to the Ever-Vital Hall where Zetian slept, and encircled it in guard service.
translations.idiomatic: Zhan followed to the Xuanwu Gate, cut through the barrier and entered, and led his troops straight to the Ever-Vital Hall where Empress Zetian slept, encircling it in guard service.

sentences.zh: 因奏：「臣等奉令誅逆賊易之、昌宗，恐有漏洩，遂不獲預奏，輒陳兵禁掖，是臣等死罪。

translations.literal: He thereupon memorialized: "Your servants received orders to execute the rebellious villains Yizhi and Changzong; fearing leakage, we could not obtain prior memorialization and rashly arrayed troops in the forbidden inner quarters—this is your servants' capital crime."
translations.idiomatic: He then memorialized: "We received orders to execute the rebellious villains Yizhi and Changzong. Fearing leakage, we could not memorialize in advance and rashly arrayed troops in the forbidden inner quarters. This is our capital crime."

sentences.zh: 」則天謂湛曰：「卿亦是誅易之軍將耶？

translations.literal: " Zetian said to Zhan: "Are you also a military general executing Yizhi?"
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Zetian said to Zhan: "Are you also one of the generals executing Yizhi?"

sentences.zh: 我於汝父子恩不少，何至是也！

translations.literal: The favor I have shown you father and son is not small—how could it come to this!"
translations.idiomatic: The favor I have shown your father and you is not small. How could it come to this!"

sentences.zh: 」則天移就上陽宮，因留湛宿衛。

translations.literal: " Zetian was moved to the Shangyang Palace, and therefore Zhan was left to guard overnight.
translations.idiomatic: " Empress Zetian was moved to the Shangyang Palace, and Zhan was left to guard her overnight.

sentences.zh: 中宗即位，拜右羽林大將軍，進封趙國公，加實封通前滿五百戶。

translations.literal: When Zhongzong succeeded to the throne, Zhan was appointed Right General of the Forest of Feathers, advanced to Duke of Zhao state, and given actual enfeoffment reaching five hundred households in all with what had gone before.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhongzong succeeded to the throne, Zhan was appointed Right General of the Forest of Feathers, advanced to Duke of Zhao, and given actual enfeoffment bringing his total household grant to five hundred.

sentences.zh: 頃之，復授左散騎常侍，累轉左領軍衛大將軍。

translations.literal: Soon he was again given the post of Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and was repeatedly transferred to Left General of the Army Guard.
translations.idiomatic: Soon he was again appointed Left Regular Attendant of the Cavalry and rose in stages to Left General of the Army Guard.

sentences.zh: 開元初卒。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Kaiyuan he died.
translations.idiomatic: He died early in the Kaiyuan era.

sentences.zh: 崔義玄別有傳。

translations.literal: Cui Yixuan has a separate biography.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Yixuan has a separate biography.

sentences.zh: 史臣曰

translations.literal: The historiographer says
translations.idiomatic: The Historiographer's Comment

sentences.zh: 史臣曰：許高陽武德之際，已為文皇入館之賓，垂三十年，位不過列曹尹；

translations.literal: The historiographer says: Xu of Gaoyang in the Wude period was already a guest whom the Literary Emperor brought into his household; for nearly thirty years his rank did not exceed director of a bureau or magistrate;
translations.idiomatic: The historiographer writes: Xu of Gaoyang in the Wude period was already a guest whom the future Emperor Taizong brought into his household. For nearly thirty years his rank never rose above director of a bureau or magistrate;

sentences.zh: 而馬周、劉洎起羈旅徒步，六七年間，皆登宰執。

translations.literal: yet Ma Zhou and Liu Ji rose from travelers on foot in bondage, and within six or seven years both reached chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: yet Ma Zhou and Liu Ji rose from travelers on foot in humble circumstances, and within six or seven years both reached chief minister.

sentences.zh: 考其行實，則高陽之文學宏奧，周、洎無以過之，然而太宗任遇相殊者，良以高陽才優而行薄故也。

translations.literal: Examining their conduct and achievements, Gaoyang's literary learning was vast and profound, and Zhou and Ji could not surpass him; yet the reason Taizong's employment and favor differed so was truly because Gaoyang's talent was superior but his conduct was thin.
translations.idiomatic: Examining their conduct and achievements, Gaoyang's literary learning was vast and profound, and Zhou and Ji could not surpass him. Yet the reason Emperor Taizong favored them so differently was truly that Gaoyang's talent was superior but his conduct was thin.

sentences.zh: 及屬嗣君沖暗，嬖妾奸邪，阿附豺狼，窺圖權軸，人之凶險，一至於斯。

translations.literal: When it fell to a successor lord who was dull and dark, with favorite concubines and wicked ministers, he fawned on wolves and jackals and spied on the pivot of power—human viciousness reached this point.
translations.idiomatic: When it fell to a successor who was dull and dark, with favorite concubines and wicked ministers, he fawned on wolves and jackals and spied on the pivot of power. Human viciousness reached this point.
